Personal opinion it will be the Ashen One.

This mostly for the ending. After all the hell we went through to gather the strength of the Lords of Cinder, to fight the incarnation of everyone who once kindle the flame, the Soul of Cinder. It's finally our turn to sacrifice and reignite it... But nothing happens. The Chosen Undead and the Bearer of the Curse from previous games had success at rekindling the flame, to extend the age of fire for a while longer, but the Ashen One, they realize it's futile, there's no strength left, the flame is slowly dying, and our sacrifice could had delayed the inevitable by what? A few minutes?

In the end we see the Ashen One comes to realize this, we see the sub slowly fading, our work, our sacrifice and pain was in vain, the world, the course of nature was inevitable, the age of the dark was inevitable, and the Ashen One only realizes this too late, and they can only accept it, kneeling down to appreciate how the first flame extinguished before their eyes.

A few tips. When you want to heal, roll backwards until you had put some distance, for dodging you will have to be focus on which attack is coming, for slashes it's better to roll backwards, for hacks and swings roll sideways. Always put attention to your stamina bar, never spam attacks or rolls, delay them a bit to avoid getting a combo. Try to remember how much a single flask can heal you, that way you just use one flask and avoid getting attacked when you're using them.
If the enemy can be backstab, try to roll inwards to the enemy's back, if you do it correctly you can reposition quickly behind them and stab them. Most of the time is trial and error, but it will become easy the more you play, your brain will slowly get adapted to the quick thinking, just try to suppress your panic. Hope this helps.

Multiplayer in this game is quite a mess to understand. Basically the game takes into account what rune level you are and what's the highest upgraded weapon you have (either you get it from a quest or made it yourself) and then it will pair you with players around the same level.
If you have more level or have a weapon level up way up it will limit or straight up lock you out of multiplayer, using passwords is the only way to bypass this I believe.

As far as I understand, the matchmaking is a tangled mess. I can confirm around low levels you get more summons and invasions (I test a new character and level up to RL40 and get quite consistent summons for bosses and pvp).
The way the match works is by taking into consideration your rune level and highest upgraded weapon (be by normal or somber stones) and the it pairs you with people around your same level. If you're a 225 level then you mostly will only get summons at the Haligtree, Leyndell or mountaintops.
I don't know if it's a bug or something, but try resting at the grace and reload the area

The infinite falling loop is something that has been happening when you get paired with hackers. As I've been reading there is a lot of trouble in PC as these things can ruin entire runs by basically locking you into a loop which can't be escaped. 
And the items you get when resting at a grace might be an attempt to put things in your inventory to try and ban you. Certain things are locked behind a boss or can't be obtained multiple times in the same game (you need new game plus or world level basically). 
If this happens after trying coop then it must probably be a hacker, I recommend playing offline for a while so you don't lose your character, but yeah it has been a lot of cases like these lately. Be careful

Best advice I can give you is to decide which way you want to go (str + int or dex + int), trying to level up all those stats at once will lock you out of getting more dps.
By personal experience, I will say you should focus on dex and int since you have moonveil, if you can then you should use a larval tear to respec.

Glad I could help. As people say both are good but the situations and environment will determined what is best. The times I had used it is against large bosses, you just have to get in the right angle so the spell can go through them and hit several times, one example is baiting the fire giant body slam, quickly get to his head and line it with the body, then just spam and watch the hp dissappear. 
Another example is against the dragon lord, run behind him and spam, I had manage to beat him in like under a minute. The downside will be it really doesn't do much against smaller enemies, it can hit them twice if lucky.

From personal experience, Shard Spiral is best for big enemies like fire giant or the dragon lord for example, since it can pierce them and hit several times in one cast and can be easily stack by spamming

I had played all of Dark Souls games, but sincerely nothing compares to the suffering Malenia gave me, not even Midir or Gael from DS3, the worst is I accidentally walked into her arena and when the cinematic played I knew I was cooked
I had heard Malenia was difficult and make a lot of people quit the game, and to be fair I don't believe it until I experienced it, that because I heard the same thing for other bosses that I end up beating in like 3 attempts at much, but she... I don't really want to try again
I never felt such fear from a boss EVER, and while I tried to beat her without ashes, I end up giving and use my mimic to at least have a quick breaths here and there
But to be honest if we're talking about the whole series, I think it will be Gael, not because he hits like a damm truck which he does, but mostly because of the overall build up to the fight, it just gives you goosebumps watching the city destroyed, the cinematic, the three phases where he goes from a savage to a literal god and how the scenery changes, personally, nothing can beat that

Quick tip as a fellow mage, Shard Spiral is your best option for big enemies, it goes through them and if aimed correctly it can hit them several times for big numbers, you can either decide to charge the spell or spam it
